مَضُوفٌ Beset by distress of mind: (TA:) [accord. to Freytag, as from the Deewán of the
Hudhalees, constrained to seek refuge: (see also مُضَافٌ:)] it occurs in the saying of the Hudhalee, “أَنْتَ تُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ المَضُوفِ
” [Thou answerest the prayer, or call, of him who is beset &c.]; and is formed after the manner of بُوعَ for بِيعَ. (M, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
